Claim 1 (Currently amended): A method of cementing comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin derived from an inulin processed from chicory; and allowing the cement composition to set.

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

Claim 3 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed under wellbore conditions.

Claim 4 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

Claim 6 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 600 or higher.

Claim 7 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin having a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.4.

Claim 8 (Currently amended): The method of claim 7 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.4.

Claim 9 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.2 to about 5 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

Claim 10 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

Claim 11 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a subterranean formation.

Claim 12 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore.

Claim 13 (Currently amended): A method of cementing in a subterranean formation comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin derived from an inulin processed from chicory; placing the cement composition in the subterranean formation; and allowing the cement composition to set therein.

Claim 14 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

Claim 15 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed under wellbore conditions.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition.

Claim 17 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

Claim 18 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 600 or higher.

Claim 19 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin having a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.4.

Claim 20 (Currently amended): The method of claim 19 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.4.

Claim 21 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.2 to about 5 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

Claim 22 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

Claim 23 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore.
